summary: EcoPulse Kerala is an interactive Earth observation analytics dashboard developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to evaluate 20-year hydro-climatic shifts and micro-climate thermal stress across two contrasting ecological zones in Kerala, India: the Idukki Highlands (Western Ghats) and the Alappuzha Coast (Arabian Sea). Powered by live satellite telemetry from the NASA POWER API v2.0 (2005–2025), the platform uses Python, Streamlit, and Plotly alongside non-parametric Mann-Kendall trend tests and Theil-Sen slope estimators to analyze precipitation, root zone soil moisture, mean temperature, and extreme heat-humidity stress. Our findings reveal statistically significant warming across both regions, with the coastal belt warming roughly 30% faster (+0.045 °C/year) than the montane highlands (+0.03472 °C/year). By transforming raw NASA satellite data into accessible geospatial insights, EcoPulse Kerala supports regional climate resilience, agricultural water planning, and ecological monitoring.
details:
EcoPulse Kerala is an interactive Earth observation analytics dashboard that tracks 20-year hydro-climatic shifts (2005–2025) and micro-climate thermal stress across two contrasting ecological zones in Kerala, India: the Idukki Highlands (Western Ghats, ~1,500m elevation) and the Alappuzha Coast (Arabian Sea, ~1m elevation). The app fetches live daily satellite telemetry via the NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER API v2.0 (0.5° × 0.625° grid) across key parameters including Corrected Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), Root Zone Soil Moisture (GWETROOT), Mean Air Temperature (T2M), and Daily Thermal-Humidity Stress (T2M_MAX ≥ 31°C and RH2M ≥ 70%).

Statistical Engine & Key Findings: Using Python (Pandas, NumPy, and PyMannKendall), the dashboard runs non-parametric Mann-Kendall monotonic trend tests alongside Theil-Sen robust slope estimators to separate statistically significant climate signals from natural inter-annual variability. Our analysis reveals that both regions are experiencing statistically significant warming, with the Alappuzha Coast warming at +0.045 °C/year (p < 0.0001)—roughly 30% faster than the Idukki Highlands (+0.03472 °C/year, p = 0.0102).

Benefits, Creativity & Intended Impact: By pairing rigorous hydro-climatic trend analysis with interactive Plotly time-series charts, Carto geospatial mapping, and a transparent data provenance audit tab, EcoPulse Kerala translates raw NASA satellite data into actionable insights for agricultural water planning, coastal heat resilience, and ecological conservation—hosted completely free and open-source for zero-barrier public access.

Tools, Languages & AI Disclosure: Developed using Python, Streamlit, Plotly, Carto, Pandas, NumPy, PyMannKendall, and GitHub, and deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud. Large Language Model (LLM) assistance was utilized during development to help structure code, documentation, and text descriptions in accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines.
